citeAs: Goyal, N., Gao, C., Chaudhary, V., Chen, P.-J., Wenzek, G., Ju, D., Krishnan, S., Ranzato, M., Guzmán, F., & Fan, A. (2021). The FLORES-101 Evaluation Benchmark for Low-Resource and Multilingual Machine Translation. arXiv preprint arXiv:2106.03193.
creator: Naman Goyal, Cynthia Gao, Vishrav Chaudhary, Peng-Jen Chen, Guillaume Wenzek, Da Ju, Sanjana Krishnan, Marc’Aurelio Ranzato, Francisco Guzmán, Angela Fan (Facebook AI Research, LORIA)
description: The FLORES-101 evaluation benchmark consists of 3001 sentences extracted from English Wikipedia (Wikinews, Wikijunior, and WikiVoyage) and professionally translated into 101 languages to enable the evaluation of many-to-many multilingual machine translation models.

name: FLORES-101
rai:annotatorDemographics: Sentence selection was performed by 10 annotators (6 male, 4 female; researchers and program managers from East Asia, South Asia, Southern Europe, Latin America, and North America). Translations were performed by professional translators from Language Service Providers.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Translation quality was assessed through a Translation Quality Score (0-100 scale) based on errors identified by evaluation LSPs (grammar, punctuation, spelling, capitalization, addition/omission, mistranslation, unnatural translation, untranslated text, register). The acceptable translation quality score was set to 90%.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For each target language, sentences are translated by a translation Language Service Provider (LSP). The resulting translations are automatically checked. If these checks fail, translations are sent back for re-translation. If the automatic checks pass, translations are sent to another LSP for human evaluation. If the quality is not sufficient, translations are sent back to the original translation LSP for re-translation.
rai:dataBiases: The authors acknowledge the potential for 'translationese' (overly literal or awkward translations) but conjecture these effects are marginal for low-resource languages. To avoid bias coming from the document structure, they carefully selected one paragraph per document, equally distributed from the beginning, middle, or end of the articles.
rai:dataCollection: Sentences were sourced from English Wikipedia (Wikinews, Wikijunior, and WikiVoyage). An article was selected at random from each source, and 3 to 5 contiguous sentences were manually selected from one paragraph per document. These sentences were then translated into 101 languages by professional translators from Language Service Providers (LSPs).
rai:dataCollectionRawData: English Wikipedia articles from Wikinews, Wikijunior, and WikiVoyage.
rai:dataLimitations: The test set is not publicly released and is only available via an evaluation server to guarantee equivalent assessment of models and reduce overfitting.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to foster progress in low-resource machine translation, benefiting the majority of the world's population who speak low-resource languages and would benefit from improvements in translation quality on their native languages.
rai:dataUseCases: Evaluation of many-to-many multilingual machine translation models, document-level translation, multi-modal translation, and multilingual classification.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Automatic checks included language identification, length checks, translation fluency according to a language model, and checking whether the translation is a copy of the translation produced by publicly available translation engines using spBLEU.
